I disagree, I think we should be in parity with https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Password_Storage_Cheat_Sheet.html

These values are very future-proof and will be solid recommendations for a decade as Moore's laws go.

We also see stable IETF standards here. https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/draft-ietf-kitten-password-storage-07

Since the industry has stabilized on what is good password storage crypto and it's not an issue of flux, specific suggestions are appropriate.

If this was seriously in flux as it was years ago, that's a different matter, but we are very stable in these recommendations as an industry.

So instead of burning down all of 2.4.x I am asking for a simple change.


2.4.4 | Verify that if bcrypt is used, the work factor SHOULD be as large as verification server performance will allow, with a minimum of 10 and consideration for bcrypt's 72-byte limit. (C6) |   | ✓ | ✓ | 916 | 5.1.1.2
